The manganese (Z = 25) has the outer configuration :-
questions.explanation:
A: Question Explanation

The question asks for the correct representation of the outer electron configuration of manganese (Mn), which has an atomic number of 25. The options show different ways of filling the outermost s and d orbitals.

B: Given Data

Atomic number of manganese (Z) = 25

C: Concept

To determine the electron configuration, we need to follow these rules:


\t
\tAufbau Principle: Electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy.
\t
\t
\tHund's Rule: Within a subshell, electrons individually occupy each orbital before any orbital is doubly occupied, and all electrons in singly occupied orbitals have the same spin.
\t
\t
\tPauli Exclusion Principle: No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers.
\t


The electron configuration of manganese (Z=25) is 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d5. The outer configuration involves the 4s and 3d subshells.


\t
\t4s subshell has one orbital, which can hold a maximum of 2 electrons.
\t
\t
\t3d subshell has five orbitals, each of which can hold a maximum of 2 electrons.
\t


Following Hund's rule, the five electrons in the 3d subshell will individually occupy each of the five d orbitals with the same spin before any pairing occurs. The two electrons in the 4s subshell will pair up in the single 4s orbital.

D: Final Answer

The correct representation of the outer electron configuration of manganese (Z=25) is:


\t
\t4s orbital: ↑↓
\t
\t
\t3d orbitals: ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑
\t

This corresponds to option (2).
